To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
hydrogen production by the pure Clostridum butyricum can be enhanced by increasing the liquid-to-gas transfer rate.

(i) the mass transfer conditions have to be taken into account to improve the biohydrogen yields, (ii) the dissolved hydrogen concentration should not be neglected, and (iii) the Henry constant has to be revised.

(1) hydrogen production was improved with a higher liquid-to- gas hydrogen transfer resulting in (2) a lower dissolved hydrogen in the culture medium, and (3) therefore in a lower inhibition of hydrogen producing bacteria.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the improvement of hydrogen production by C. butyriucum CWBI10009 through the control of mass transfer conditions.
the development of new tools to enhance hydrogen yields and rates by the pure strain C. butyrium CWBI1009, which could be applied to other strains.
the improvement of hydrogen production by C. butyrium CWBI1009 and the development of a new model to predict the hydrogen production rate and yield.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hydrogen production is not inhibited by its own hydrogen gas production, but rather by the dissolved hydrogen concentration in solution.
hydrogen production was enhanced by a higher mass transfer coefficient, which led to a lower dissolved hydrogen level in the medium.
hydrogen production by C. butyicium is not inhibited by its own production, but that its rate and yield are limited by the mass transfer conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hydrogen production by Clostidium butylicum was enhanced by the increase of the mass transfer coefficient.
the mass transfer conditions have a significant influence on the performance of biohydrogen production, especially for the pure strain Clostidium butyrcium.
hydrogen production yield and rate were enhanced by the addition of stirring up to 200 rpm and nitrogen bubbling in the AnSBR and in the BHP tests.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of the pure strain C. butyriculum CWBI1009, in combination with a better liquid-to-gas transfer, can be an efficient strategy to improve hydrogen production.
mass transfer conditions should be considered in the design of biohydrogen production processes.
the dissolved hydrogen concentration is a key parameter to consider in biohydrogen production processes.
